sources.title: Resumable upload protocol 1.0.x
sources.locator: Core Protocol and Headers; OPTIONS and Protocol Extensions; Creation; Expiration; Checksum; Termination
sources.observed_operation: Read the normative protocol text and examples for HEAD/PATCH continuation, creation, extension advertisement, expiry, checksum, and delete termination.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Core is mandatory; extensions are optional and must be announced in Tus-Extension. HEAD provides current offset; offset mismatch requires 409 without mutation; successful PATCH returns new offset. Expiry is optional and communicated by Upload-Expires; checksum applies per PATCH; termination is optional and DELETE should free resources.
sources.applicability: Direct protocol basis for a gateway-facing resumable HTTP option. Auth, URL shape, persistence backend, and idempotent creation are implementation-defined; do not infer vendor storage behavior from Tus.

sources.title: Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic release/version shown (accessed 2026-10-10)
sources.locator: Multipart upload process, lines 23-41; multipart listings and checksums, lines 51-69; cleanup note, lines 33-36
sources.observed_operation: Read the AWS-described initiate/upload/complete flow, part bookkeeping, listing, checksum validation, completion, and abort race/cost notes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AWS uses an upload ID and part number; completion requires the client's part number/ETag list. ETag is not necessarily a whole-object MD5. A supplied full-object checksum is validated server-side; mismatch fails BadDigest. In-flight part calls can still finish around abort; parts incur storage charges until complete/abort.
sources.applicability: Normative evidence only for Amazon S3. The brief's vendor is unspecified and merely S3-compatible, so all API, checksum, cost, and abort claims require exact-provider conformance testing.

sources.title: Amazon S3 multipart upload limits
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic release/version shown (accessed 2026-10-10)
sources.observed_operation: Read maximum object, part count, part-number, part-size, last-part exception, and ListParts page-size limits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AWS limits part size to 5 MiB–5 GiB, except the final part may be smaller; maximum 10,000 parts; ListParts returns at most 1,000 per request.
sources.applicability: AWS S3 limits only. A proposed 16 MiB sizing plan fits the AWS values for 20 MiB–6 GiB; confirm target-service limits before adoption.

sources.title: Aborting a multipart upload
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic release/version shown (accessed 2026-10-10)
sources.locator: Opening paragraphs and cleanup guidance, lines 3-9; abort ID behavior, lines 73-84
sources.observed_operation: Read multipart object visibility, storage charges, explicit abort, and lifecycle cleanup behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: No completed object exists until CompleteMultipartUpload succeeds; incomplete part storage remains billable until completed or aborted; bucket lifecycle can clean incomplete MPUs. Abort by upload ID/key makes that upload ID unusable.
sources.applicability: AWS S3 only. Equivalent expiry/abort/lifecycle semantics for the unnamed compatible vendor are unknown.

sources.title: Announcement: S3 default integrity change, aws-sdk-rust issue 1240
sources.released_version_or_commit: AWS SDK for Rust S3 client v1.69.0; maintainer announcement posted 2025-01-16. Issue does not specify a commit.
sources.locator: Issue description, paragraphs 1-3; page showed issue Open at access
sources.observed_operation: Read maintainer release/default announcement and compatibility caveat.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: From v1.69.0 the Rust SDK defaults to an additional checksum on Put calls and validation on Get calls. Maintainers warn AWS SDKs target AWS and third-party services may not yet support newly enabled defaults; configuration can set request_checksum_calculation/response_checksum_validation to WHEN_REQUIRED.
sources.applicability: Relevant if the gateway or a future Rust component uses this SDK against a compatible service. It supports a pinned, endpoint-specific adapter and test boundary, not disabling integrity by default; exact gateway SDK/provider are unknown.

sources.locator: Issue description and reproduction, paragraphs 1-7; logs around CompleteMultipartUpload
sources.observed_operation: Read one reported multipart completion failure and its stated environment/log evidence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter said larger uploads failed at completion with InvalidPartOrder; reproduction cites AWS S3 and tusd latest. The posted evidence does not establish root cause or whether all configurations/versions are affected; no fix is established by this page.
